question: Which statement best describes Static metadata export?
options: When metadata depends on data — a product name, a blog post title — export an async `generateMetadata({ params })` function instead of a static object. It runs on the server, can `await fetch`, and returns the same `Metadata` shape. Next dedupes fetches shared with the page so you don't fetch twice.

Set `title.template` in a layout (e.g. `'%s | Acme'`) and child pages provide only the `%s` part via `title.default` or a plain string. This gives consistent, brand-suffixed titles across the site without repeating the brand on every page. Use `title.absolute` to opt out of the template.

The `openGraph` and `twitter` fields control how links look when shared on social platforms — title, description, and preview image. Next emits the right `og:` and `twitter:` meta tags. You can also generate dynamic preview images with the `opengraph-image` file convention.

Export a `metadata` object from a `layout.tsx` or `page.tsx` and Next renders the corresponding `<head>` tags on the server. It's typed (`Metadata`), merges down the route tree, and is the simplest way to set a page's title, description, and social tags when they don't depend on data.
explanation: Export a `metadata` object from a `layout.tsx` or `page.tsx` and Next renders the corresponding `<head>` tags on the server. It's typed (`Metadata`), merges down the route tree, and is the simplest way to set a page's title, description, and social tags when they don't depend on data.
